question.text: Category I and II AIFs must be:

answer.text: Close-ended with a minimum tenure of three years
Either open or close-ended at manager's discretion
Close-ended with a maximum tenure of one year

explanation.text: The Logic: Category I and Category II AIFs shall be close-ended, and the tenure of each scheme is determined at the time of the SEBI application, subject to a minimum tenure of three years. This close-ended structure reflects the illiquid nature of alternative investments — Category I and II AIFs are described in the workbook as illiquid, so investors may not be able to exit until winding up and distributions are completed, with any earlier exit limited to fund-document transfer/withdrawal practices or secondary-market sale of unit capital or partnership interests. The Trap: Only Category III AIFs can be open-ended. The three-year minimum applies to the scheme's tenure, and any later extension is governed by the separate extension rule rather than turned into an open-ended structure. Note: Kept the close-ended three-year minimum key. Removed the unsupported pro-tip claim that most funds have 7-10 year tenures, and softened the 'no early exit route' wording to source-backed illiquidity plus limited secondaries/transfer routes.
